title: Tail latency playbook + standup notes (Mar 13 2026)
summary: Working notes from the perf/benchmark sync focused on recurring tail-latency spikes under mixed short/long request workloads. We reviewed three experiments (kv-cache pressure, batching heuristic variance, warmup slot shortage), captured intermediate metrics, and agreed on next steps: increase warmup slots for canary hosts, tighten batching thresholds for mixed sequences, and add a KV cache eviction profiler.
content:
Attendees: Asha (owner), Diego, Sana, Jonah, Priya, Evan
Meeting context: weekly perf sync + ad-hoc triage after customer-reported p99 volatility in hosted region eu-west-1 on 2026-03-11. Notes are intentionally informal — capture hypothesis threads and quick test logs.

Agenda:
- Quick recap of incident / customer report
- Results from three isolation experiments run 2026-03-12 18:00-20:30 UTC
- Discuss hot paths (kernel selection / scheduling / kv-cache)
- Decide immediate mitigations and medium-term invest tasks

1) Incident recap (customer-facing symptom):
- Customer A: sudden p99 jumps from ~210ms -> ~420ms for short-chat seqs (~64 tokens) during a mixed-workload hour window (spike lasted ~14m). Throughput reduced ~27% vs baseline.
- No error rates elevated; tail-only latency phenomenon.
- Incident correlated with an internal spike in long-sequence (8k) generation requests from a different tenant in same capacity pool.

2) Experiment summary (isolation runs)
- Run A: KV-cache pressure simulation (seq variety: 80% short(16-64), 20% long(4k-8k), sustained qps 320).
  - Config: rw-13b-v1-q4, batch cap 32, max_batch_delay_ms 8, prefix_kv_cache enabled (default eviction LRU).
  - Observations: p50 ~45ms (no change), p95 up 15%, p99 up 65% vs baseline. Cache hit-rate dropped from 94% -> 71% at 12m mark. CPU on host +8% due to extra KV recompute and memory pressure on GPU memory manager.
  - Hypotheses: frequent KV cache churn causing extra recompute paths and longer schedule stalls for short requests.

- Run B: Batching heuristic tweak (more aggressive early flush for mixed sequences).
  - Config change: reduce batching threshold for short sequences from 24 tokens to 12 tokens, reduce max_batch_delay_ms 8 -> 4.
  - Observations: p99 improved ~18% relative to Run A (but still +30% vs baseline). End-to-end throughput ~ -6% (expected due to smaller batches). Tail jitter reduced but didn't fully recover.
  - Notes: CPU scheduling overhead rose slightly; kernel switch counts per request increased (recorded in tracing).

- Run C: Warmup-slot increase on canary pool (warmup_slots 2 -> 6 for canary hosts; prefetch KV prefixes observed).
  - Observations: Coldstart count fell to near-zero during sustained load; p99 down to within 10% of baseline; throughput recovered to ~95% baseline. Warmup improvement most effective when combined with batching tweak.

3) Microprofiling nuggets (collected from tracing and flamegraphs):
- Context switch stalls correlate with KV eviction window (approx 18-22ms microbursts every ~120s under mixed workload).
- Kernel recompile or selection events are rare in these runs; kernel-selection not primary cause.
- Docker cgroup reclaim activity observed on one host (we're pointing that instance out for infra repro).

4) Immediate mitigation proposals (agreed):
- Short term (0-24h):
  1) Roll warmup_slots bump (2->6) for canary pool in eu-west-1 (owner: Jonah, ETA: 2026-03-13 T14:00 UTC).
  2) Push a conservative batching heuristic change for mixed workloads to staging (owner: Diego, ETA: 2026-03-14). Use flag gated rollout.
  3) Add observability: emit per-host prefix_kv_cache hit-rate metric with 1s granularity (owner: Sana, ETA: 2026-03-15).

- Medium term (1-3 weeks):
  1) KV cache eviction profiler and trace correlation tool (owner: Evan, ETA: 2026-03-30). Will store samples to s3 run bucket for deeper analysis.
  2) Batching heuristics experiment matrix (owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-03-27). Matrix to sweep max_batch_delay_ms {2,4,8,12} and short-seq threshold {8,12,24}.
  3) Investigate cgroup memory reclaim interactions with GPU memory manager (infra handoff to infra-team, Miro contact: infra pager).

5) Test-run logs (rough scribbles)
- run-2026-03-12-A (kv-pressure): qps target 320, sustained 14m, p50 46ms p95 128ms p99 391ms, cache_hit 71%, coldstarts 4
- run-2026-03-12-B (batching): qps target 320, sustained 10m, p50 48ms p95 110ms p99 321ms, cache_hit 73%, coldstarts 3.
- run-2026-03-12-C (warmup-high): qps target 320, sustained 18m, p50 46ms p95 98ms p99 234ms, cache_hit 92%, coldstarts 0.

6) Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does cache_hit degrade so sharply under pressure? Is it placement (same host) or policy (LRU not ideal for mixed seqs)?
- Can we make a fast-path that bypasses KV recompute for short seqs when a recent prefix exists on host? (Sana to sketch API impact)
- How much throughput are we willing to trade for tail reduction in hosted tier? Need product guidance for SLO tradeoffs.

7) Decision notes:
- No immediate rollbacks of kernel changes. Evidence points to cache churn + warmup shortage as combined root cause.
- Proceed with canary warmup slot bump + conservative batching rollback gate.

8) Action items (copied here for visibility):
- Jonah: bump warmup_slots on eu-west-1 canary hosts, monitor p99 and cache_hit metric; report by 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC.
- Diego: open PR for batching flag + benchmark in staging (include perf harness config), target 2026-03-14.
- Sana: instrument prefix_kv_cache hit-rate; add Grafana panels for heatmap by host; target 2026-03-15.
- Evan: prototype kv-eviction profiler; store traces to s3 run bucket and link in this doc; target 2026-03-30.
- Priya: own batching sweep matrix, run in shadow against production trace; target 2026-03-27.

9) Quick follow-ups for next sync (2026-03-16):
- Review canary metrics (Jonah + Sana)
- Inspect initial sweep results for batching (Priya + Diego)
- Check infra host that showed cgroup reclaim (Asha to loop infra on 2026-03-13)

Notes-to-self: keep this doc as a living capture. If you paste run logs into s3, drop a link under linked_artifacts. We should convert successful mitigation steps into the Tail Latency Playbook page on Confluence and add a short runbook snippet for on-call to try (warmup bump + temporary batching flag).

End of notes.
